lines.label: B1
lines.reason: 90 deg fold from base plate 1 into a+ wall 3. Full-resolution perpendicular sections every 2.5 mm put the line on the outer-skin arc. Offset is -0.35 to +0.42 mm (station_median line, slightly bowed arc), 0.01 / 0.27 / -0.27 mm at 25/50/75%. The wall leg is present from t=0 to 267.5 mm and missing just past both ends, so the line covers the whole wall (~268 mm). The capped legs seen in some sections are holes or notches near the fold, not breaks in it.

lines.label: B2
lines.reason: 90 deg fold from base 1 into a- tab 5/6. Outer apex offset is -0.12 to +0.04 mm at every station. The tab leg runs t=0 to 107.5 mm and the line spans the full tab width. It is collinear with B3 but sits on a separate tab across a ~90 mm bare plate edge. That gap is a separate flange, not a window or relief, so a second line is correct.

lines.label: B3
lines.reason: 90 deg fold from base 1 into a- tab 8/9, the second separate tab. Outer apex offset is -0.07 to +0.15 mm. The tab leg runs t=0 to 70 mm and the line covers the full tab width (~70 mm).

lines.label: B4
lines.reason: 90 deg fold from base 1 down into upper Z wall 7 (b+ side). Outer apex offset is -0.22 to +0.04 mm. The wall leg runs t=0 to 202.5 mm and is missing beyond both ends, so the line covers the full wall (~202 mm). The inner-skin cap at 50% is the large hole in wall 7, not a break in the fold.

lines.label: B5
lines.reason: Joggle bend 1: 90 deg fold from upper wall 7 inward into the ~9 mm step (underside 12). The line is on the convex outer arc, -0.09 to +0.03 mm off at every station. Both legs are present from t=0 to 202.5 mm and the line spans the full step length.

lines.label: B6
lines.reason: Joggle bend 2: real 90 deg fold from the step down into lower wall 10/11. Lines.json uses the concave inner skins 11/12 for this fold. At most stations the convex outer skin (step top and inner face of the lower wall) is occluded. My sections find the inner-skin apex 1.35 mm inward along the bisector. At the stations where outer-arc points were scanned, the outer apex is 0.45-0.6 mm outward (median ~0.52, one station 0.99). Inner apex plus t=1.92 also puts the outer apex ~0.57 mm out. So the line sits ~0.5 mm inside the sheet from the outer apex: parallel, under the 1 mm OFFSET threshold, but not exactly on the skin. The lower-wall leg runs t=0 to ~190 mm and is missing beyond that (the step continues), so the extent matches the lower wall (~190 mm).
